explanation: Searched Mathlib for any statement connecting `Set.projIci`/`projIcc` (or a general monotone-identity projection) with `Measure.map` and `Integrable`: grep over `projIci`, `projIic`, `projIcc` in Mathlib only finds the order-theoretic definition/lemmas in `Mathlib/Order/Interval/Set/ProjIcc.lean` (and a topological path lemma); there is no measure-theoretic `map_..._projIci` statement. Also searched for the generic integrability primitives used (`integrable_map_measure`, `integrable_add_measure`, `integrable_smul_measure`, `integrable_dirac`) and for candidates like `integrable*Ioi`, `integrable*Iic`, `Integrable ... max`, `restrict_Ioi`/`restrict_Iic` decompositions — none states integrability under the projected law `μ.map (projIci l)` being equivalent to integrability on `μ.restrict (Ioi l)`. Mathlib's closest general tool is `integrable_map_measure`, but reducing this theorem to it would require decomposing `μ` into `restrict (Iic l) + restrict (Ioi l)` and proving `f ∘ max l · =ᵐ f` on `Ioi l`, i.e. an argument of substance, not a one-line instantiation. The library's own proof in fact goes through its own lemma `map_coe_projIci`, so the mathematical content is library-specific.
